description: "Use when editing the Streamlit app, Streamlit support helpers, or their tests. Covers session isolation, background crawl jobs, progress/cancel events, downloads, and container startup."
applyTo: "apps/streamlit/**"

# Streamlit App

Browser UI for users who prefer a form-based crawl workflow.

## Related Skills

- Before Streamlit app work, read `.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/SKILL.md`.
- Load the relevant Streamlit sub-skill from `.agents/skills/` for the specific task, such as layout, session state, performance, CLI, markdown, or design work.

## Constraints

- `apps/streamlit/streamlit_app.py` owns the shared app shell and global Streamlit session state. Keep crawl/job helpers in `apps/streamlit/src/app_support/support.py`.
- Page modules live under `apps/streamlit/app_pages/`. They must expose `render_page()` and render content-area UI only.
- When a page needs shell-owned callbacks or shared runtime state, pass a small context object from `streamlit_app.py` into the page module instead of importing `streamlit_app.py` from the page module.
- The shell delegates two rendering clusters to top-level `app_support` modules: the **Output Files** panel to `downloads_ui.py` (`_render_downloads`, `_render_ready_result_panel`) and the **live progress** areas to `progress_ui.py` (`_render_live_area`, `_render_vector_index_live_area`, plus `_apply_vector_index_event`). Shared UI constants, the job-state vocabulary, and shell helpers (`_session_root`, `_job_is_alive`, `_active_file_root`, cached file discovery, `_auto_refresh_fragment`, …) live in `app_runtime.py`. Import direction is one-way: `streamlit_app.py`, `downloads_ui`, and `progress_ui` all import from `app_runtime`; nothing imports `streamlit_app.py`. Event draining (`_drain_job_events`), app-wide toasts (`_emit_crawl_progress_toasts`), and the crawl event loop (`_render_crawl_event_loop`) stay in the shell.
- Prefix page-specific session keys with the page id when adding complex state to Steps 2-5, for example `vector_index_*` or `basic_rag_qa_*`.
- `app_support.support` must not import Streamlit. Keep it pure Python so it stays unit-testable.
- Deployment-tunable, non-secret config lives in `app_support.settings` (`pydantic-settings` `Settings` + cached `get_settings()`), loaded from `.env.defaults` (committed) then `.env` (git-ignored) then the process environment. `Settings` fields are **required** with no in-code fallbacks, so `.env.defaults` is the single source of truth for every default (a missing key fails fast). The form/UI default constants (`form_defaults`, `vector_form_ui`, `llm_form_ui`), the app download/preview limits, the semantic-search top-N, and the session-retention window read from it; keep the libraries pure (no env reads beyond cloud auth). Secrets (`AWS_*`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) stay plain environment variables — `.env` locally, root-level keys in `.streamlit/secrets.toml` on Streamlit Community Cloud — never in `settings`.
- **Anti-bot escalation (Step 1)** is deployment-configured, not per-crawl form input: `build_configs` reads `proxies` from the `CRAWL_PROXIES` secret env; undetected-browser escalation is automatic on retry rounds (no setting). `start_crawl_job` builds an optional scraping-API fallback from `CRAWL_FALLBACK_API_URL`/`CRAWL_FALLBACK_API_TOKEN` and passes it to `SiteCrawler(fallback_fetch_function=...)`. The crawler uses each paid resource at most once per crawl (by default proxy on the first retry, API on the second; set `CRAWL_PROXY_ON_INITIAL=true` to also proxy the initial crawl for sites that block the first unproxied request) and logs per-URL usage to `logs/network_usage.csv`. Proxies and the fallback API are secrets — env / `.streamlit/secrets.toml` only, never `.env.defaults` or logs.
- **Signed zip upload:** Output Files' subtitle links to an upload dialog; downloads are HMAC-signed (`build_folder_zip_bytes(signing_secret=ZIP_SIGNING_SECRET)`), uploads verified with `verify_zip_bytes` and re-imported under a conflict-free name via `import_signed_zip` (artifact_store). A bad signature shows an error; success toasts via the shell pending-toast pattern. The **Sample data** panel (under File Details, collapsed) one-click-imports the bundled `data/fixtures/` crawl/index archives into the session via `import_sample_fixture` — trusted repo files extracted with the shared `_extract_zip_to_new_folder`, no signature check.
- The multipage shell uses native `st.navigation` in `streamlit_app.py`. Keep `app_support.pages` pure; it owns page metadata only and must not import Streamlit. `st.navigation` is registered on every run *before* the session-bootstrap `st.stop()` gate so deep-linked page URLs (e.g. `/vector-index`) survive hydration reruns; do not move it back below the gate.
- The shared page shell renders the title/subtitle, session controls, language selector, page content, footer, and portfolio modal. Do not duplicate any of these inside page modules.
- App-wide notifications, including progress toasts that should appear on every workflow page, belong in the shared shell rather than individual page modules. Do not call `st.toast()` in `apps/streamlit/app_pages/**`; if a future page needs an app-wide toast, pass a shell-owned callback/context. Keep page-local feedback inline with page content (`st.info`, `st.warning`, `st.success`, or page panels).
- **Steps 3-5 — Semantic Search / RAG Q&A / Conversational RAG** are implemented and inherit the shared page shell. Each page receives a `RagPageContext` from the shell (`default_language`, `list_indexes`, `render_downloads`) and renders an explicit **index picker** built from `index_catalog.list_session_indexes` (pure: discovers successful indexes under the session root). All RAG logic lives in the UI-independent `rag_engine` library (`retrieve`, `answer_question`, `chat_answer`); pages are thin and only collect input, call it, and render the structured `RagAnswer`/`RetrievalResult`. RAG runs **synchronously**, not as a background job (Steps 3-4 use a spinner; Step 5 drives a live `st.status` from `conversational_answer`'s `progress_callback`, localizing `rag.progress.*` stage messages).
  - **Step 3 (Semantic Search)** selects an index first (wrapped in a card), shows its `manifest.json` metadata inside that card in a collapsible **:material/info: Metadata** expander (collapsed by default) as a compact **4-column grid** via `render_index_metadata` (built from the pure `index_metadata_rows` helper, including the manifest `created_at` formatted in local time via `generated_files.format_local_datetime`), runs a search (the query + a top-N number input + Search button live in a form; the top-N defaults to `settings.semantic_search_top_n` and flows into a plain closest-match `RagConfig`), and renders ranked result cards via `render_result_cards` inside an always-present collapsible **Search results** panel (`render_results_panel`, which shows a neutral title + hint when empty; when there are hits the title carries the match count plus a `:material/leaderboard:` icon, collapsed by default and auto-expanded only right after a search; the last hits persist in `semantic_search_results` session state so the panel survives reruns; it leads its cards with the query via `render_results_panel`'s optional question heading) — one collapsed **expander per hit** (`:material/article:` icon + a `#{rank} • {source}#{chunk} • {score}%` title from `result_panel_title`, collapsed by default so long result lists stay compact); expanding a hit reveals its `Chunk #{n} · size · language` caption then the chunk text in **Raw/Preview** tabs — Raw first by default, configurable via `SEMANTIC_SEARCH_DEFAULT_TAB`, each tab's text wrapped in its own card so the tabs read as UI — from the pure `result_detail_caption`/`ordered_result_tabs` helpers, sorted score-descending). Every search (direct or replayed) appends a `SearchRecord` to the session's `search_history/` folder via the pure `search_history` module (JSONL + downloadable CSV, capped at the most recent 200; each record also embeds the returned hits as `StoredResult` snapshots — `rag_shared/result_snapshot.py` — plus the elapsed search time, so each history card shows a **results / search time** Metadata row and re-renders its own collapsed **Search results** panel via `chunks_from_stored`); a collapsed **Search history** expander below the form lists past searches newest-first as a **card list** — each card leads with the query, a right-docked pin toggle + replay button (`:material/keep:` ↔ `:material/keep_off:` via `set_search_pinned`, the pin turning **primary/accent** while pinned; pinned records sort first, then newest-first; `:material/replay:`), then a collapsed **:material/info: Metadata** expander holding a compact 4-column grid (time via `generated_files.format_local_datetime`, result count, source index, and the index fields broken out — embedding model, language, dimension/chunks, chunk size/overlap — enriched from the live manifest when it still exists); the replay button replays the query + Vector DB selection by pre-filling the keyed widgets across an `st.rerun` and moves focus to the query field. It ends with the shared Output Files section (`context.render_downloads()`), mirroring Step 2. Leave `render_sources` (used by Steps 4-5) unchanged. The pure card helpers (`render_result_cards`, `result_detail_caption`, `ordered_result_tabs`) live in `rag_ui` and are unit-tested in `test_rag_ui.py`.
  - Steps 4-5 share the chat-model list from `llm_form_ui` (`chat_model_choices` → `resolve_offered_from_pricing`), **driven by `config/model_pricing.yaml`** filtered to the `RAG_LLM_SIZE_BANDS` bands (XS/Small by default) intersected with the `rag_engine` callable catalog; the default comes from `RAG_DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL`, and `RAG_LLM_MODELS` + `resolve_chat_model_choices` stay the fallback when that config is missing/empty. `chat_model_label` reads `provider · name · cloud service · size band` from the pricing config (catalog label fallback otherwise). **Step 4 (Basic RAG Q&A)** is a bespoke two-stage page: a bordered panel (Vector index + Top results, Language model + Tone; tones/default from `BASIC_RAG_QA_TONES`/`BASIC_RAG_QA_DEFAULT_TONE`, top results from `BASIC_RAG_QA_TOP_RESULTS`), a single-line question → **Generate prompt** (retrieval renders its hits in an always-present collapsible **Search results** panel between the question and prompt — `retrieve` runs under a `BASIC_QA_SEARCHING` spinner, then the shared `render_results_panel` shows them **collapsed** with the match-count title, led by the question via its optional `question` heading — with `rag_engine.build_rag_prompt`, whose prompt template comes from `basic_rag_qa_form_ui.resolve_basic_rag_qa_prompt_template(session_root)` — a per-session saved template (from the **Edit template** editor) → the `BASIC_RAG_QA_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_FILE` file (a customer-service persona by default) → the built-in library default — into an editable prompt field with an icon-only **Maximize** form-submit button that opens a large (height-capped) `st.dialog` editor with an explicit **Apply** button that writes the edit back to the inline prompt (via the pure `basic_rag_qa_form_ui.apply_maximized_prompt`) and closes; dismissing another way (X / click-away / Esc) discards the edits); an **:material/edit_note: Edit template** button on the left of the question panel (with **Generate prompt** on its right; both are form-submit buttons — Generate is placed in the *first* column so Enter submits Generate not Edit, and the button row is visually reversed with scoped `flex-direction:row-reverse` CSS so Edit still shows on the left) opens a height-capped `st.dialog` over the resolved template, where **Save** — validated for the `{question}/{start}/{knowledge}/{end}/{tone}` placeholders by `basic_rag_qa_form_ui.basic_rag_qa_template_is_valid` — persists it to `basic_rag_qa_history/prompt_template.txt` for the session (`save_basic_rag_qa_template`) and **Reset to default** removes it (`reset_basic_rag_qa_template`), so the next Generate uses it), and **Send** (`rag_engine.stream_prompt` → `st.write_stream` rendered in an **Answer** sub-panel inside the prompt form under the button, with a token/latency caption that names the model used). It logs each send via the pure `basic_rag_qa_history` module (`basic_rag_qa_history/`, JSONL + CSV; each record also embeds the retrieved hits as `StoredResult` snapshots and the split search/answer timing) rendered as tidy cards mirroring Step 3's Search history — with a collapsed **Search results** panel between the Metadata and Prompt expanders (`chunks_from_stored`) and a Metadata **Search + answer** timing row shown as `search + answer = total` seconds — a question label + right-docked pin & replay buttons (the pin accent-colored while pinned), a collapsed **:material/info: Metadata** 4-column grid, and a collapsed **:material/description: Prompt** expander showing the exact sent prompt, and a collapsed **:material/forum: Answer** expander showing the returned answer with its model/token/latency caption (replaying a card reloads its question, prompt, and options), with a collapsible **Token usage** panel (collapsed by default; metrics carry Material icons, and a nested **Transaction history** table lists each request's date/time, model, token counts, and process) above the history showing `basic_rag_qa_form_ui.token_totals` as Input / Output / Total then a `BASIC_RAG_QA_SESSION_TOKEN_QUOTA` budget as Quota and Usage (`basic_rag_qa_form_ui.usage_percent`, floored, display-only). **Step 5** uses the same bordered panel as Step 4 (Vector index + Chunks, Answer model + Tone) built inline in `render_advanced_controls` (`select_index` + `chat_model_choices` + `tone_choices`; tones/default from `BASIC_RAG_QA_TONES`/`BASIC_RAG_QA_DEFAULT_TONE`, threaded into `ConversationalConfig.tone`), and is a chat UI (`st.chat_message`/`st.chat_input`) with history in `st.session_state` and history-aware query rewriting from `rag_engine`. All RAG pages (Steps 3-5) render their heading + caption with plain `st.subheader` + `st.caption` to match Steps 1-2, for consistent spacing.
  - **Step 5 (Conversational RAG)** drives the advanced `rag_engine.conversational_answer` pipeline over a bottom-pinned `st.chat_input`; user bubbles right-align (messenger-style). Controls mirror Step 4 (Vector index + **Top results** — the former "Chunks" field, Page-4 help/default 5 — Answer model + Tone) plus an **:material/tune: Advanced options** panel whose tabbed **prompt-template editor** lets users edit + Save + Reset each of the six LLM-stage prompts (answer / decompose / rerank / followups / answerability / state); resolution precedence is session-saved edit → app config `.txt` (`config/conversational_*_prompt.txt`, dir `CONV_RAG_PROMPT_TEMPLATE_DIR`) → library constant, resolved into a `rag_engine.ConversationalPrompts` via `conversational_rag/conversational_prompts.py` (mirrors Step 4's Edit-template save/reset; a bad override falls back inside the library). Per-turn timings/models render **inside** the collapsed **🔎 Inspect this turn** expander (no always-visible strip). A conversation control row (a **:material/add:** New button + a picker) groups the session's turns into independent **conversations**: each persisted turn (`conversational_rag_history/`, JSONL+CSV) carries a `conversation_id` + `transaction_id` + the rewriter's `state_summary`, so re-opening a session rehydrates the picker and — on selection or session load — replays that conversation's turns **from disk** as display-adequate `ConversationalAnswer`s (no live retrieval cache; state seeded from the persisted summary **plus** an `asked_questions` history rebuilt from the saved turns (`asked_questions_from_records`) so follow-up de-dup survives a reload) via `conversational_rag/conversation_manager.py` (`new_conversation_id`/`new_transaction_id`, `conversation_title` = rolling-summary-else-first-question truncated, `conversation_summaries`, `conversation_turns`, `turn_from_record`, `asked_questions_from_records`, `trim_old_turn_payloads`). To bound a long chat's memory only the most recent `CONV_RAG_MAX_LIVE_TURNS` (default 30) turns keep their retrieved-chunk payloads live; older turns keep their Q/A text but shed `sources`/follow-up chunks (`trim_old_turn_payloads`), staying reachable via the picker. The active id lives in `conversational_rag_current_id` (a plain key the shell clears on session switch so a switched-to session re-defaults to its own most-recent conversation), and the picker is a **keyless, index-controlled** `st.selectbox` (diff its return against the active id to switch — do not bind a widget key). A **Token usage** panel — the shared `rag_shared/token_usage_ui.py` renderer (`TokenPanelData` + `render_token_usage_panel` + `format_cost`, also used by Step 4) fed by `conversational_rag/conversational_token_ui.py` aggregating each turn's per-process `StageTokenUsage` (quotas `CONV_RAG_SESSION_TOKEN_QUOTA` / `CONV_RAG_SESSION_COST_QUOTA`; the Step 5 table shows **millisecond** transaction times via `local_time_label(…, with_seconds=True)`, **merges** a turn's repeated same-`(process, model)` stages into one `N× …` row via `CONV_PROCESS_MULTI`, and adds **Conversation ID** / **Transaction ID** columns) — and the shared **Output Files** section (`context.render_downloads()`) both render below the chat.
  - Prefix Steps 3-5 session keys with `semantic_search_` / `basic_rag_qa_` / `conversational_rag_`. The shell hands RAG pages a `RagPageContext` (`list_indexes`, `render_downloads`, `session_root`). Localize `rag_engine` warnings/errors with `i18n.localize_message` (codes `rag.*`); never substring-match library text. New RAG UI strings live in `i18n/en.py` + `i18n/id.py` (and the `Strings` TypedDict). Cloud embeddings keep the `☁️‣🔑` tag (needs an API key; the picker's help text points to the README); chat models instead show `provider · name · cloud service · size band` from the pricing config, and the RAG Q&A answer caption names the plain model label (`Model — …`, no tag).
  - **Model pricing & cost (`app_support.model_pricing` + `config/model_pricing.yaml`).** The YAML is the single source of chat-model display metadata (provider, cloud service, size band) and USD prices per 1M tokens; a model with no published price yields `None` from `estimate_cost` (shown as `n/a`). It drives the Step 4/5 picker (size-band filter + label; see above) and the **Token usage** panel: every metric shows a token/count on top and its USD figure below as a neutral delta (`delta_color="off"`) — Input/Output/Total costs, the static Quota (token budget / `BASIC_RAG_QA_SESSION_COST_QUOTA` cost budget), and Usage (token % + `$` %, cost ÷ cost quota via `cost_usage_percent`). The nested **Transaction history** table adds **Provider / Cloud service / Est. cost (USD)** columns (Date & time uses a three-letter month), a **Pricing** preview button (`:material/request_quote:`, opens a read-only `render_pricing_markdown` table) left of the **Download CSV** button, and a source-cited estimate **disclaimer** caption below the table. Keep pricing/metadata in the YAML — never hardcode per-model figures in the page. A new model id must be added to both the `rag_engine` catalog (callable) and the YAML (priced/labelled); `test_model_pricing.py` asserts every priced id is callable.
  - **Dialog dismiss + toast + sample import.** Step 4's Maximize / Edit-template dialog actions (**Apply**, **Save**, **Reset to default**) run inline (`if st.button(...): handler(); st.rerun()`) so the dialog closes and a page toast (`_PAGE_TOAST_KEY`, fired by the shell) shows immediately — do not rely on an `on_click` callback for dialog-closing actions (its fragment-scoped rerun skips the shell toast check). The **Sample data** import (`downloads_ui._import_sample_fixture_action`) likewise ends with `st.rerun()` so its folder-naming success toast fires.
- **Step 2 — Build Vector Index** is implemented and mirrors Step 1's shell. The page (`app_pages/vector_index.py`) receives a `VectorIndexPageContext` from the shell and only collects form input and calls callbacks. Indexing logic lives in the UI-independent `vector_indexer` library; the background job lives in `vector_index/vector_index_jobs.py` (mirrors `crawl/crawl_jobs.py` — thread + event queue + cooperative cancel). Do not put indexing business logic in the app.
  - Prefix Step 2 session keys with `vector_index_` and keep them separate from crawl keys. Reuse the shared `dialog_ui.render_confirm_dialog` helper with its own handler, `vector_stop_*` button keys, and **vector-specific wording** (`VEC_DIALOG_STOP_BODY`/`VEC_DIALOG_BTN_STOP` — "Stop indexing", never the crawl strings); do not modify `crawl/crawl_jobs.py` or the crawl stop handler.
  - Reuse the existing output-files display (`_render_downloads`) and the form action buttons (`crawl_action_buttons`); the form lives in `vector_index/vector_form_ui.py` with pure, testable option/validation helpers (`crawl_result_options`, `has_index_inputs`, `resolve_embedding_model_choices`). The embedding-model dropdown order and pre-selected default are operator-tunable via `VECTOR_EMBEDDING_MODELS`/`VECTOR_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` (validated against the library's `EMBEDDING_MODEL_OPTIONS`; default `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, listed first).
  - Vector outputs are written under `outputs/streamlit_sessions/session_<id>/vector_<id>/<timestamp>/`. Build the base with `session_manager.prepare_vector_output_base`; discover crawl inputs with `artifact_store.crawl_results.list_crawl_result_files`.
  - **Cross-browser indexing lock + progress.** `vector_index/vector_index_jobs.py` keeps a process-local registry (`_VECTOR_JOB_REGISTRY` + `_REGISTRY_LOCK`, `VectorJobSnapshot`) mirroring `crawl/crawl_jobs.py`: `start_vector_index_job` registers a snapshot that the worker updates on every emit (`_update_snapshot`), exposed via `get_active_vector_job_snapshot` / `active_vector_registry_session_ids`. The shell reattaches an in-progress index after a browser refresh (`_reattach_selected_session_vector_job`, replaying the latest event to seed stage/progress/result), `_start_vector_index_job` reattaches instead of launching a duplicate when a snapshot is already alive, and the startup cleanup unions `active_vector_registry_session_ids()` so an actively-indexing session is never pruned. The reattached running state locks the Step 2 form via `_current_vector_runtime` `fields_disabled`. `_select_session_id` resets the `vector_index_*` keys on session switch so the target session reattaches its own job.
- Keep `session_id` and `crawl_id` separate. Browser sessions write under `outputs/streamlit_sessions/session_<id>/crawl_<id>/`.
- **Transient results clear on session switch.** `_select_session_id` calls `app_support.session_reset.clear_transient_result_state(st.session_state)` so a created/switched-to session never shows the previous one's Step 3 search hits or Step 4 generated prompt/answer. The cleared key names live in `session_reset` (app_support must not import `app_pages`); a parity test (`test_session_reset.py`) keeps them in lock-step with the page modules. When a page adds a result/answer key, add it there too.
- All file access for generated outputs must stay inside the session root. Use the existing path validation helpers instead of manual string checks.
- Background crawls should use `start_crawl_job()` and communicate through queue events. Do not block Streamlit reruns while a crawl is active.
- Cancellation must stay cooperative through `SiteCrawler.should_cancel`; do not terminate threads forcibly.
- Progress UI should consume crawler event mappings and helper estimates. Keep event keys stable unless tests and Streamlit consumers are updated together. Step 1 progress cards carry a leading icon via `st.metric(icon=…)` (Streamlit 1.61) — the five count metrics use Material icons and the state metric uses the status emoji; keep every metric's `icon` set.
- **Live statistics persistence.** The crawl Live-statistics expander stays open after a crawl finishes or is stopped, not only while it runs: `_live_area_expanded(job_state, latest_event)` returns True when the job is active **or** `latest_event` holds data, so the final counts stay visible (they persist in `latest_event`, which resets only on session switch or a new crawl). Keep this behavior — do not tie the expander to active job states alone.
- Downloads should come from the generated-file listing helper and respect the app download-size guard. Each file row's label shows the file name plus its human-readable size via `generated_files.format_file_size` (e.g. `sorted_success_content_001_of_001.md • 5.9 MB`). Folder rows in the download tree pick a Material icon by artifact type via `generated_files.download_folder_icon` (`crawl_*` → `:material/travel_explore:`, `vector_*` → `:material/database:`, `search_*` → `:material/search:`, otherwise `:material/folder_open:`). History folders (`search_history`/`basic_rag_qa_history`) additionally show their **created timestamp** in the panel label via `generated_files.format_history_folder_label` (parsed from the first record in `<folder>.jsonl`, e.g. `search_history/2026-07-12_04-21-46 (12 July 2026 14:21 AEST)`). The cached file discovery in `app_runtime` uses `@st.cache_data(refresh_mode="background")` and the file table renders with `st.dataframe(lazy=True)` (Streamlit 1.61).
- **Files actions disable during jobs.** While a crawl or vector-index job is active (`_files_actions_busy` = `_crawl_job_active() or _vector_job_active()`), the 📁 Files & folders action buttons (Import, Export, Delete this folder, Preview, Download) stay **visible but disabled** instead of hidden, so a user cannot mutate outputs mid-write. Import always renders (disabled while busy) rather than being hidden. The panel itself stays visible whenever no job runs (`downloads_ui._should_show_files_panel`), even before the session folder exists, so Import is reachable after a browser reset clears the session; during a job it appears only once it holds files.
- **Explore a crawl in 3D (`site_graph_3d/`).** Each `crawl_*` folder's action row (right of **Export**) — and the **📦 Crawl results ready** panel beside **Download** (50/50 columns; the CCv2 button stretches to match Download via `render_explore_3d_button(full_width=True)`) — gets a **:material/bubble_chart: Explore in 3D** control (the folder's `site_graph.jsonl` is located via `generated_files.find_site_graph_file` in the download tree, or `find_site_graph_for_result` from a ready download's `<crawl>/<ts>/…` path) that opens a self-contained Three.js "universe" of the crawl in a **new tab** (planets = pages sized by weight / surfaced by richness / coloured by status with rings for large pages — **failed pages render as asteroids** (dark, irregular rocky bodies whose lumpy shape and cratered surface are procedurally generated per page URL — a displaced `IcosahedronGeometry` with a seeded canvas texture (`makeAsteroid`/`makeAsteroidNoise`) — so every failed page looks distinct; they emit no light and stay below the bloom threshold, reading as dead rock; the scene uses a single global bloom that lights the suns and the trajectory lines), seed page = central sun; pages are laid out **in the browser** by a **d3-force** simulation (`assets/viewer.js`; positions are no longer computed in Python) — pages repel, parent→child links attract, and collision + centre-gravity keep the whole crawl compact, so a large, deep site reads as clustered constellations with the seed page pinned as the central sun; links = discovered-from, each carrying a lone **electron** drifting back and forth (random per-edge timing/direction) while unselected — except a link to a **failed page**, painted **red** (`FAIL_LINK`, via a precomputed `failEdges` set keyed on `color_category === "fail"`) so each asteroid is easy to trace back to its parent; hover shows details + lights the chain to the root, click opens a side panel with the record + a live iframe that falls back to an "open in new tab" link when the site blocks framing). Ambient motion (planet spin, starfield drift, and a slow whole-scene camera auto-revolve at `AUTO_ROTATE_SPEED`) is idle-gated in `viewer.js` through an eased `idleFactor` and only plays after `IDLE_MS` (10 s) of no interaction, gliding to a stop on interaction. It opens the crawl's **published static file** (written by `site_graph_3d.static_publish` to `apps/streamlit/static/orrery/<session_id>/<crawl>_<ts>_<lang>.html`, served at the `app/static` URL via `server.enableStaticServing`) in a **new tab** from an inline **CCv2** button (`launcher.py`, `component_v2`); the click stays inside the user gesture and the tab is **refreshable and shareable** (unlike the previous blob URL). A raw static file — not a registered Streamlit page — keeps the full-screen feel (no shell chrome). `launcher.py` rebuilds the document only when stale (`orrery_needs_refresh` vs the graph mtime); published files are namespaced by the unguessable session id and pruned with their session (`remove_orrery_static`, called from `_run_startup_cleanup`). Trade-off: static files are readable by anyone with the link — an accepted cost for a refreshable URL. The viewer opens with **Controls collapsed** and the title already reading **Site Orrery** (no fallback flash). Keep the split: pure, Streamlit-free, unit-tested helpers shape and assemble everything (`graph_data` → node/edge model, `viewer_assembler` → self-contained HTML, `viewer_labels` → EN/ID viewer text) from the frontend assets under `assets/` (`viewer.*`, `launcher.*`); only `launcher.py` imports Streamlit. Do not push visualization logic into `crawl4md` — the library only emits `site_graph.jsonl`. three.js loads from a **pinned** CDN (`viewer_assembler.THREE_VERSION`), and injected graph JSON is `<`-escaped to block `</script>` breakout. The button honours `_files_actions_busy()`. The panel button's label/tooltip are i18n keys (`FILES_EXPLORE_3D_LABEL`/`_HELP`); in-viewer labels live in `viewer_labels` (parity-tested), not the i18n catalog, because the viewer is a standalone tab rather than Streamlit-rendered UI.
- **Folder zip export (on-demand modal).** Each top-level `crawl_*`/`vector_*` run folder — plus the fixed `search_history` and `basic_rag_qa_history` folders (`generated_files.is_history_folder`) — gets an **Export** button (`:material/folder_zip:`) at the start of its action row, before its **Delete this folder** button (a `crawl_*` folder's **Explore in 3D** control sits between them). It does **not** build the zip on render (a large vector DB would balloon memory on every rerun); instead it sets `export_folder_relative_path` and opens an `@st.dialog` (`_export_folder_dialog`). The dialog builds the archive **once**, uncached, inside an `st.spinner` via the pure `generated_files.build_folder_zip_bytes(session_root, relative_path)` (full contents nested under the folder name, validated with `ensure_within_root`, refusing the session root, as `<folder>.zip`), holds the bytes in `export_zip_payload`, renders an `st.download_button`, and auto-starts the download by clicking it once via `focus.click_widget` (guarded by `export_autoclicked`; a visible button is the fallback). It reuses the app download-size guard (`UI_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT_MB`) — oversized folders show a "too large" message. Do not reintroduce an eager per-render build or an `@st.cache_data` folder-zip wrapper. `build_folder_zip_bytes` is unit-tested in `test_generated_files.py`. **History import (replace-in-place):** a signed `search_history`/`basic_rag_qa_history` zip uploaded via the Import dialog replaces that history folder through `generated_files.import_history_zip` — whitelisted to those two folder names so a crafted zip can't overwrite crawl/vector output (zip-slip-safe); an upload always confirms first — a warning when that history already exists (`generated_files.history_exists`, replace-in-place), otherwise a plain confirmation. Keep the whitelist — never extend in-place overwrite to arbitrary top folders. Both helpers are unit-tested in `test_generated_files.py`.
- **Per-session logging.** `log4py.configure_logging` runs once per process (`@st.cache_resource` `_configure_app_logging`) with `logger_names=_PROJECT_LOGGER_NAMES` and a `log_file_router=_session_log_path` (not a fixed `log_file`). Each record routes to `session_dir(<current session>)/<settings.log_file>` chosen from a `contextvars.ContextVar` (`app_support.log_context`); the shell sets it per run after bootstrap-ready (`set_log_session_id`) and **each background job thread sets it as the first line of `run()`** because threads do not inherit contextvars. The session log is surfaced in the 📁 Files & folders panel as a preview+download row next to the Import button (`_session_log_generated_file`, merged into the tree deduped). Pre-session records (before a session is selected) go to stderr only. Do not revert to a single global `logs/app.log`.
- **Folder delete + shared confirm dialog.** Each top-level `crawl_*`/`vector_*` run folder — and the fixed `search_history`/`basic_rag_qa_history` folders — in the download tree gets a red **Delete this folder** button (gated on `generated_files.is_run_folder` or `is_history_folder`) that opens an `@st.dialog` confirmation driven by `delete_folder_relative_path` and calls the pure `generated_files.delete_generated_folder(session_root, relative_path)` — it validates with `ensure_within_root`, refuses the session root, `shutil.rmtree`s the folder, and prunes emptied parents. All confirm dialogs (crawl stop, vector stop, folder delete) share `dialog_ui.render_confirm_dialog` (green keep + red right-docked confirm) so look/UX stays consistent; only the `@st.dialog` wrapper, dismiss handler, and callbacks differ. The pure `confirm_dialog_css`, `is_run_folder`, `is_history_folder`, `find_site_graph_file`, and `delete_generated_folder` helpers are unit-tested. The two scrollable content modals — the file **Preview** (`downloads_ui`) and the model **Pricing** table (Step 4) — share `dialog_ui.scrollable_dialog_css(scope, content_key)`: it widens the dialog to ~70% and stretches a keyed `st.container(height=…)` to `70vh` so the body scrolls **inside** the modal. Use it (not deep `nth-child` dialog-DOM selectors, which broke on a Streamlit upgrade) for any new sized/scrollable modal; the editor dialogs (Maximize / Edit template) keep their own wider `90vw` sizing since they hold a text area, not a scroll container.
- **Session retention** is configurable via `settings.session_retention_days` (`SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 7). `_run_startup_cleanup` passes it into `cleanup_old_sessions_with_lock`; do not hardcode the window. `cleanup_old_sessions(retention_days=...)` keeps `_DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` only as a fallback default.
- The dev container starts Streamlit on attach at `0.0.0.0:8501`. If the port or startup command changes, update `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `README.md`, and `devcontainer.instructions.md` together.
- Tests must use `tmp_path` and mocked/stubbed crawl jobs. Never make real network requests from Streamlit tests.
- Streamlit tests follow the Streamlit Tests policy in [tests.instructions.md](./tests.instructions.md).
- **Translation catalog:** Whenever new user-facing text is added to the Streamlit UI, add both an English and an Indonesian entry to the `apps/streamlit/src/app_support/i18n/` package first — `en.py` and `id.py` — then reference the key via `get_strings()` in the UI code. Never hardcode text directly in Streamlit components. **Library messages** (crawl/index warnings and errors) arrive as structured `LibraryMessage` data with a stable `code`; localize them with `i18n.localize_message` against `MESSAGE_CODES` (EN+ID), falling back to the library's English `default_text` — never substring-match library error text in the app. To add a new language, create a new `<code>.py` file in the package and register it in `__init__.py`.
- **Load Session dialog:** The 📁 button in `streamlit_app.py` (`_load_session_dialog`) lets users paste a session ID to restore access from another browser or device. When the dialog opens, the session-ID field auto-focuses via `focus.focus_widget` (a one-shot `_focus_session_id` flag). Session IDs are validated with `validate_safe_id()` before any server-side path is constructed. `touch_session()` must be called after a successful load to reset the retention clock (`SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 7). The dialog must stay disabled while a crawl is running.
